## Why peyesim?

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}

### Fixations to densities
Kernel density estimation with configurable bandwidth and multiscale support, designed for typical eye-tracking spatial scales.
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.card .h-100 .p-3}
### Template similarity
Compare encoding and retrieval gaze with permutation baselines, scanpath comparison, and cross-recurrence summaries.
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.card .h-100 .p-3}

A faithful port of the R `eyesim` package — same APIs, same outputs, tested against an R oracle.
:::
:::

## In 30 seconds

::: {#a24dd726 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import numpy as np
from peyesim import fixation_group, eye_density, similarity

fg1 = fixation_group(
    x=np.random.uniform(0, 100, 25),
    y=np.random.uniform(0, 100, 25),
    onset=np.cumsum(np.random.uniform(0, 100, 25)),
    duration=np.random.uniform(50, 300, 25),
)
fg2 = fixation_group(
    x=np.random.uniform(0, 100, 25),
    y=np.random.uniform(0, 100, 25),
    onset=np.cumsum(np.random.uniform(0, 100, 25)),
    duration=np.random.uniform(50, 300, 25),
)

ed1 = eye_density(fg1, sigma=50, xbounds=(0, 100), ybounds=(0, 100))
ed2 = eye_density(fg2, sigma=50, xbounds=(0, 100), ybounds=(0, 100))
similarity(ed1, ed2, method="pearson")
```
:::
